summary.title: ClawGUI: A Unified Framework for Training, Evaluating, and Deploying GUI Agents

details: GUI agent progress is bottlenecked by missing full-stack infrastructure rather than modeling capacity: online RL pipelines are closed and emulator-only, evaluation configurations drift silently across papers making numbers incomparable, and trained agents rarely reach real users on real devices.

ClawGUI, an open-source end-to-end harness with three integrated modules: ClawGUI-RL (online RL infrastructure with a unified device abstraction covering parallel Docker Android emulators and real physical devices, combining outcome reward with a Process Reward Model for dense step-level supervision under GiGPO's hierarchical advantage estimation), ClawGUI-Eval (decoupled Infer→Judge→Metric pipeline with per-model pinned evaluation configurations and released raw predictions), and ClawGUI-Agent (deployment harness with hybrid CLI-GUI control and persistent personalized memory across mobile OSes and chat platforms).
ClawGUI-2B initialized from MAI-UI-2B; 64 parallel virtual environments (MobileWorld Docker Android emulators) on 8x A6000 48GB GPUs
GiGPO with rollout group size 8, temperature 0.7, lr 1e-6, 3 epochs, train batch size 8; max 50 interaction steps
Qwen3.5-72B as PRM judge scoring each action given previous/current screenshots plus action history; reward R = R_outcome + R_step

Environment manager: task reset, system-level (root) verification plus MLLM-as-judge, spare-server rotation on unhealthy containers, periodic teardown; real-device training relies on hand-authored tasks and MLLM-as-judge only (no root access)
Trainer built on verl / verl-agent with support for PPO, Reinforce++, GSPO, GRPO, GiGPO
MobileWorld GUI-Only split (117 interactive real-world mobile tasks, visual control only), metric = Success Rate
Baselines: MAI-UI-2B/8B, GUI-Owl-7B/32B, UI-Venus-7B/72B, Qwen3-VL-8B/32B/235B, Doubao-1.5-UI-TARS, plus agentic frameworks (GPT-5 / Gemini-3-Pro / Claude-4.5-Sonnet + UI-Ins-7B)
Ablation: GRPO (episode-level binary reward) vs GiGPO (episode + step-level dense reward)
6 benchmarks: ScreenSpot-Pro, ScreenSpot-V2, UI-Vision, MMBench-GUI, OSWorld-G, AndroidControl
11+ model families reproduced (GUI-G2, GUI-Owl 1.5 2B/4B/8B, Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, UI-TARS 1.5, UI-Venus/1.5, MAI-UI, StepGUI, Gemini 3.0/3.1 Pro, Seed 1.8)

Success criterion: reproduced >= official or |delta| <= 2%; local transformers inference plus OpenAI-compatible API backend, multi-GPU multiprocessing with shard checkpointing; benchmark-specific judges (point-in-box, polygon/refusal-aware, multi-action)
Closed-source frontier models evaluated via a two-stage Zoom (crop-then-ground) paradigm: 25% crop tiles for Gemini, 50% for Seed
Android, HarmonyOS, iOS targets; 12+ chat platforms (Feishu, DingTalk, Telegram, Discord, Slack, QQ) in remote or local control mode
Memory: structured facts (contacts, frequent apps, habits) stored as vector embeddings, top-k retrieval into system context, duplicate merging
ClawGUI-Eval exposed as an agent skill triggerable by a single natural-language benchmarking command

key_findings.finding: A 2B agent trained end to end in the released RL infrastructure surpasses its same-scale base model and much larger untrained GUI models on an interactive mobile benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: ClawGUI-2B reaches 17.1% Success Rate on MobileWorld GUI-Only (117 tasks) versus 11.1% for the identical-weight base MAI-UI-2B, and above Qwen3-VL-32B (11.9%), Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B (12.8%) and UI-Venus-72B (16.4%).

key_findings.finding: Dense step-level credit assignment materially improves GUI RL over episode-level advantage estimation.
key_findings.evidence: Ablation within the same pipeline: GRPO with binary episode-level reward gives 14.5% SR while GiGPO with episode- plus step-level dense reward gives 17.1%, a 2.6-point (17.9% relative) gain.

key_findings.finding: GUI evaluation discrepancies are largely an infrastructure/configuration problem, not intrinsic irreproducibility.
key_findings.evidence: Pinning per-model evaluation choices in the Infer→Judge→Metric pipeline reproduces 46/48 cells with official baselines (95.8%; 95.7% for open-source models, 100% for frontier models on ScreenSpot-Pro) within the |delta|<=2% or >=official criterion.

key_findings.finding: The two reproduction failures correspond exactly to models with undisclosed official evaluation configurations, implicating hidden prompt/resolution choices as the main irreproducibility driver.
key_findings.evidence: Qwen3-VL-2B (48.5 official vs 43.9 reproduced) and UI-TARS 1.5-7B (49.6 vs 42.06) on ScreenSpot-Pro are the only failures, and both lack publicly disclosed evaluation settings.

key_findings.finding: Closed-source frontier models' reported grounding numbers can be recovered without internal access using a simple two-stage crop-then-ground protocol.
key_findings.evidence: The Zoom paradigm (25% crop tiles for Gemini, 50% for Seed) yields 75.08 vs 72.70 official for Gemini 3.0 Pro and 72.80 vs 73.10 for Seed 1.8 on ScreenSpot-Pro, and 85.01 for Gemini 3.1 Pro.
